meta.title: TOEFL TPO Writing — latest tasks (TPO 66–75)
meta.scope: The 10 most recent TPO sets (TPO 66–75). Each TPO writing section has two tasks: Task 1 = Integrated Writing (read a passage, hear a lecture that responds to it, then summarize the lecture and how it relates to the reading); Task 2 = Independent Writing (an agree/disagree or preference essay).
meta.note_on_format: The live TOEFL iBT replaced the Independent essay with a 'Writing for an Academic Discussion' task in July 2023. The numbered TPO practice sets (TPO N) are compiled from earlier administered exams and still pair an Integrated task with an Independent task; the newer Academic-Discussion prompts are published by prep sites as a separate series. Both are covered by the accompanying scraper.
meta.fidelity: Prompts and topics below were verified from public prep-site pages via web search. Task 1/Task 2 PROMPT wording is verbatim (high confidence). Reading-passage and lecture bodies are SUMMARIES, not verbatim transcripts — the source sites that host the full verbatim text (top.zhan.com / 小站, lingoleap, ETS, KMF) are blocked by this environment's outbound network policy, so full bodies must be pulled with the accompanying scraper from a network-unrestricted environment. Missing fields are marked null.

integrated_writing.topic: Controlling the invasive Northern Pacific sea star (Asterias amurensis)
integrated_writing.reading_summary: The Northern Pacific sea star is native to the coasts of Japan, Korea, and China but has recently appeared thousands of kilometers away, where it threatens marine ecosystems. The reading proposes three strategies to control its spread: (1) administer a poison called quicklime (calcium oxide), spread in powdered form over invaded areas of seafloor — it destroys sea stars but is said not to harm commercially important mollusks such as oysters, scallops, and mussels; (2) introduce natural parasites that specifically attack the sea star; and (3) sterilize the ballast water of ships so the larvae are not transported to new regions.
integrated_writing.lecture_summary: The professor argues that none of the three strategies would be effective. (1) Quicklime would also kill native sea stars, which help maintain local ecosystems; it stays active on the seafloor for a long time, so native sea stars moving back into treated areas would die too. (2) A parasite effective enough to control the invaders would likely also attack native sea star species, and might not be specific to the target. (3) Sterilizing ballast water does not address sea stars that have already established populations, and the invaders can also be transported by other means, so this measure would not stop the ongoing spread.
